articles.title: Compound Eye
articles.summary: Dense hex-packed ommatidium dots, iridescent grey-green, high contrast, fine repeating organic grid. A blue and olive wallpaper with vertical wavy lines and eye-like dots, reminiscent of a 60s psychedelic or Art Nouveau wallpaper; the ovals read as small beads.
articles.what: Insect compound eye — hex close-packed ommatidium ring array Up close: Vertical columns about 32 px apart, each a stack of small concentric ovals (tan ring, green ring, dark core) joined by wavy tan lines that bulge in and out, with blue lens-shaped cells between and tiny green triangles. A fine dotted mesh runs under the blue. A seamless, regular tile in muted blue. From a distance: A blue and olive wallpaper with vertical wavy lines and eye-like dots, reminiscent of a 60s psychedelic or Art Nouveau wallpaper; the ovals read as small beads. Group: Nature, Animals & Weather. Texture detail: fine.
when: Best on: body, hood, hero panel.
how: Click a zone card and open the PATTERN section.
Click Pattern 1 on this Layer to open the picker.
Open the group "Nature, Animals & Weather" or search for "Compound Eye", then click it.
Drag Scale below 1.00 until the repeats look fine on the car.
Switch Paint mode to Blend if you want to keep your paint colour.
tips: Doors and quarters: columns run vertically, so tall panels show the wave
Hood and roof also work as an all-over wallpaper
Mid contrast and a regular tile; numbers read fine in a bold light colour.
Dark
Pairs well with: dark green, black, gunmetal.
pitfalls: Not a hex honeycomb: it is wavy columns of ovals, not six-sided cells
Not cable knit: ovals are concentric rings with a core, not linked loops
Avoid: pastel bases, small trim areas.
